invariant: ADR-0048 §3.4 retired the per-item cross-package throw because a caller carries its package id. Three families of consumers carry none, so with two holders every caller is served one package's item, picked by registration order: the data family — a field's picklist, an import's mappingName and a dashboard's datasetName — serves the first-registered one; the request family — the endpoint matcher's API, an object-less action's handler and the engine function registry's function, read by a flow script node or an action's target — serves the last-registered one; the flow family — the automation engine's one armed flow per name, the dispatcher's one declared webhook per name, the connector picker's one connector per name and a send's email template bundle — serves the first-registered one (the flow: the lexicographically-first package's, with a warning). The maintainer's ruling C on #30798 (phase 1, ADR-0048 addendum 2026-11-06, each family in its own change under #30803) narrows §3.4 for these types: one name, one PACKAGE holder. After the cold boot seals the registry (kernel:bootstrapped), a package bringing a name another installed package or a built-in holds is refused at three doors, naming both holders and the namespace-prefixed rename: the package door (SchemaRegistry.installPackage) and the item seam (SchemaRegistry.registerItem) for the registry types, and the hook binder's bind (bindHooksToEngine in hook-binder.ts, through SchemaRegistry.claimBareNameFunctions) for a function, ahead of every registration it would make. An email template's NAME holds its (name, locale) bundle, so the holder reading strips the registry key's member. ⛔ Never judge the environment catalog — an environment item under a package's name is the ADR-0005 overlay — never judge a type's overridable baseline (OVERRIDABLE_BASELINE_PACKAGES: the email service's built-in templates, which an app's same-named template overrides by contract, so that package neither holds a template name nor is refused one), never let OS_METADATA_COLLISION=warn downgrade the refusal, never judge during the boot (a deployment already holding a clash must still boot: the cold-boot switch decides warn or refuse), and never treat a package that already holds the name as a new holder.
